source.prompt: (the chestnut-backed chickadee's) A chestnut-backed chickadee (Poecile rufescens), a tiny songbird about 11 cm long, one adult perched with its wings folded tight against the body, side-on pose. A round fluffy body, a big round head, a tiny short black bill, a medium-long narrow tail. A sooty dark brown cap and a black bib, bright white cheeks, a rich chestnut back and flanks, grey wings and tail, a white belly. Thin dark legs, three toes forward and one back. No base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: A variant of the chestnut-backed chickadee's Meshy preview (no credits), scaled to 0.09 m (the round body and tiny thin bill suit it), a short notched tail of 3.5 cm (the centre pulled back, a point at each corner). Colours (the male): olive-grey back, nape and rump, paler grey-white below with olive-washed sides; the crown an orange centre stripe in a yellow stripe bordered black each side; a white eyebrow over a black eye line; grey face, pale throat; dark wings with two white wing bars (lod0 and lod1) and yellow feather edges (lod0); dark olive tail; black bill, dark legs. Triangles: lod0 1,000 = 802 body + 198 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod1 400 = 308 body + 92 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod2 120 = 90 body + 30 legs, tail, cards, eyes. GLB 187,336 bytes. lod_m is a suggestion.

rig: bird rig template of the Steller's jay (tools/build_stellersjay.py; drawn with client/src/animalModels.js RIG.stjay's constants): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 / LEG_B 2 procedural legs (pivot at the knee), TAIL 3 procedural tail (pivot at the rump), HEAD 6 (head and neck, pivot at the base of the neck), WING_L/R 4/5 and HAND_L/R 9/10 flight cards that collapse into the shoulder on pose; extras.rig {kind 'bird', wing (shoulder), tail (rump), head (neck base), length_m}; no skin
accuracy_notes: Built 2026-11-05. Reads as a golden-crowned kinglet: tiny, round, the striped orange-yellow-black crown and white eyebrow. Still open: the notch is small and only shows from above; the folded-wing bars are a few faces; male only (the female's crown is all yellow).
